newsitem.title: USA: US senators file bill to ax New England dairy pact.
newsitem.headline: US senators file bill to ax New England dairy pact.

text.p: Legislation to repeal the Northest Dairy Compact, which allows the six New England states to raise the price of milk bound for grocery stores, was filed Thursday by eleven senators.
The compact also was under challenge in U.S. district court. Judge Paul Friedman has set arguments for Feb 25 on Milk Industry Foundation suit that says the compact was improperly created.
Sponsors of the bill derided the compact as a "backroom political deal." It was included in the 1996 farm policy law during House-Senate negotiations on the final text.
"It's grossly unfair to give dairy producers of six states a competitive advantage over farmers in Minnesota and 43 other states," said sponsor Senator Rod Grams, Minnesota Republican.
The consumer group Public Voice for Food and Health Policy has estimated the compact could cost New Englanders tens of millions of dollars over its three-year life.
Proponents say the compact, which allows price increases of up to 25 percent for fluid milk, will help farmers stay in business in a densely populated, high-cost region.
Sen. Pat Leahy, D-Vt, said Congress would not want to wade into dairy so soon after passing the farm law.
